LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 SELECTIVE LISTENING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to pick out specific details during an oral presentation? 2. Why do we give instructions and directions?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. filter required information from an oral text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. take notes from an oral text or recordings on diverse topics,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. give and follow instructions for carrying out different tasks,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. ask for and give clear directions to a place for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. argue for the need to listen attentively to extract specific details.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

2. give simple, clear, effective instructions to complete tasks and activities. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm ways of selecting and noting down specific information from a listening text. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology to write.
2. give simple, clear, effective instructions to complete tasks and activities. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions and those 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Selective Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration as the learner's ability to listen keenly is enhanced as they listen to an audio on

instructions and directions and paraphrases the content.

● Digital Literacy- Using digital technology as the learner sharpens the skill of digital skills by recording themselves as

they give instructions and directions in a dialogue.

Values:
Respect is promoted as the learner observes etiquette as they play games such as cue games to enhance selective listening.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Socio-economic issues – safety and security as learners increase their knowledge by listening to a text on travel.

● Child road safety as learners shares with peers how to use emergency exits or operate the door locks of a vehicle,

especially during an accident.

Suggested Learning Resources: Dictionaries, newspapers, charts and realia, resource persons, audio recordings, adapted

digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand. universal

cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. filter required information from an oral text,
2. take notes from an oral text or recordings on diverse topics,
3. give and follow instructions for carrying out different tasks,
4. ask for and give clear directions to a place for effective communication,
5. argue for the need to listen attentively to extract specific details.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to pick out specific details during an oral presentation? 2. Why do we give instructions and directions?
